mechanism_narrative: Weekly WORKPLACES means rose in three of the last four weeks (-62.9, -56.3, -55.0, -51.3), showing commutes are resuming; resumed commutes generate incidental weekday retail trips, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 11.6 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is not higher than its mean over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has held above -66 for three consecutive weeks and reached -63.9 at t-0; once transit use crosses -65 the population has enough confidence in shared transport for discretionary trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses from below to at or above -65 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -68.4 at t-3w to -63.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the two weeks following a TRANSIT close at or above -65.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT is the operative condition: gains in either alone do not generate enough foot traffic, but simultaneous week-on-week gains in both signal a broad return to out-of-home routines that lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve versus their prior-week means in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved at t-0w versus t-1w
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve together, RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is no higher than in weeks where only one of them improves.

mechanism_narrative: Under partial-reopening rules residents are still held at home and RESIDENTIAL is declining (24.6 to 21.7); each point of residential decline converts into out-of-home hours spent disproportionately in retail and recreation, so RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below its trailing four-week mean
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.9 points from t-3w to t-0w
regime_hint: partial reopening with stay-at-home guidance still in force
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL declines further while the RETAIL_REC mean stays flat or falls over the same 28-day window.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is stable near -20 while RETAIL_REC sits near -67, a persistent 47-point gap; grocery trips prove households already shop outside the home, so the retail gap closes and RETAIL_REC gains within one week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC remains more than 40 points below GROCERY_PHARM for three consecutive weekly prints
evidence_refs: fact:gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC was 46.4 points at t-0w
failure_condition: The RETAIL_REC minus GROCERY_PHARM gap fails to narrow over the following 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS swung from 61.3 to 11.9 and back to 31.1, tracking weather rather than infection risk; because parks is a weather-sensitive outdoor channel, its latest rebound precedes a warm-weather retail and recreation upturn within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rebounds by more than 15 points from its prior-week value
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 19.2 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: After a PARKS rebound greater than 15 points, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than its prior-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL staying above +20 while WORKPLACES remains near -51 means workers remain home-based; home-based workers cannot supply the daytime retail footfall a rebound needs, so RETAIL_REC stays below its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +20 while WORKPLACES stays below -50
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 21.7 and WORKPLACES -51.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL stays above +20 and WORKPLACES stays below -50.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC improved in each of the last three weekly prints (-72.6, -70.6, -70.3, -66.7); when the four-week slope turns positive for three consecutive prints, reopening policy momentum continues and RETAIL_REC keeps rising over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC improves versus its prior-week mean for three consecutive weekly prints
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC gained 5.9 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: After three consecutive weekly RETAIL_REC improvements, the next 14-day mean falls below the prior 14-day mean.
